rst-v2-hygiene1-a-consumer-symptoms.title: From contamination to symptoms in the consumer
rst-v2-hygiene1-a-consumer-symptoms.text: Suppose pathogens contaminate food on a preparation surface. Someone who eats it may develop vomiting, diarrhea or other harm. Link food contamination with its effects on the consumer. These are examples of symptoms; everyone does not necessarily develop identical symptoms.

rst31-v2-hyg-q005.objective: Link pathogen contamination of food with possible vomiting, diarrhea and other harm to the consumer.
rst31-v2-hyg-q005.stem: After bacteria or viruses contaminate food, a customer eats it. Which describes a possible effect?
options: The person may develop vomiting, diarrhea or other symptoms
Eating the food alone makes the pathogens harmless
Food contamination has no relation to the health of the person eating it
Everyone who eats it necessarily develops exactly the same symptoms
rst31-v2-hyg-q005.explanation: Eating contaminated food can harm health. Vomiting and diarrhea are examples, not symptoms that necessarily occur identically in everyone.
reasons: It connects contaminated food with possible symptoms in the consumer
Eating alone does not make pathogens harmless
Eating contaminated food may harm health
Examples must not become symptoms required in every person
